advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Apply the pinned keyring's era boundaries (added_at/revoked_at) on the local pinned-environment path, or document why revocation is intentionally not enforced there.
evidence: src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:474-478: `return [ rec["public_key"] for rec in keyring if isinstance(rec, dict) and isinstance(rec.get("public_key"), str) and rec["public_key"] ]` — revoked_at_log_position is dropped
src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:500-502: pinned path returns `pinned, "pinned_environment"` before the envelope_key fallback, and is reached regardless of `required_env`
src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:83-84: `allowed_signers_from_keys` emits `f"{principal} {key_line.strip()}"` with no valid-after/valid-before interval
src/rebar/attest/opcert.py:209: the merge-gate path resolves `added_at_log_position`/`revoked_at_log_position` to era boundaries — the local path does not
advisory.finding: The pinned-environment trust path ignores key revocation/era boundaries. `_pinned_environment_keys` collects only `public_key`, discarding `added_at_log_position`/`revoked_at_log_position`, then `_opcert_trust_root` feeds the bare keys to `allowed_signers_from_keys(keys, principal)` which emits an allowed_signers line with no valid-after/valid-before interval. The merge gate (`verify_opcert`, via the same keyring) DOES resolve those era boundaries, so a key that is revoked in `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` still certifies on the local `verify_signature` / claim-gate path with `trust_basis == "pinned_environment"`. Because pinned is preferred over envelope_key even when `require_environment` is unset, any project with a pin file that revokes a key retains local acceptance of certs made with the revoked key.
scenarios: A project pins environment E's key, later revokes it (sets revoked_at_log_position), but the revoked key still certifies E's older op-certs on a local claim/close verification.
trust_basis reports pinned_environment for a key the trusted-env config has revoked.

The equivalent narrative in docs/concurrency.md was corrected in this same change, leaving the emitted CLI warning inconsistent with the shipped behavior.
scenarios: An operator re-clones a tracker and reads the ENV_ID_MISMATCH / re-clone warning, is told their attestations are now unverifiable and must be re-earned, but they in fact still certify — misinforming the operator and prompting needless re-signing.

evidence: src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py:195 `def embedded_public_key(signature: bytes) -> str | None:`

Branches with no direct test: `if not blob.startswith(_SSHSIG_MAGIC): return None`, `except ValueError: return None` (from `_read_sshsig_string`), and `if not keytype_str or _has_control_chars(keytype_str): return None`

The end-to-end suite only exercises a wholly-unparseable armor (b'not-an-sshsig-blob'), which hits only the base64-decode failure branch.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add unit cases feeding embedded_public_key() a base64-armored blob that (a) starts with b'SSHSIG' + a length that overruns the buffer, (b) has correct base64 but wrong leading magic, and (c) has a keytype string containing a control char, asserting None for each.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconsider the fail-open in `_required_environment`: when `verify.require_environment` was configured, an unreadable/malformed config should fail CLOSED (refuse / retain the last-known restriction) rather than silently dropping enforcement and re-enabling the envelope_key fallback.
evidence: src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:458-461: `try: return config.compose_config(root=repo_root).verify.require_environment or None` / `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — no readable config ⇒ no required environment` / `return None`
src/rebar/config.py:514-515 (compose_config): 'A :class:`ConfigError` propagates (fail-closed startup)' — the normal contract is fail-closed, which this catch overrides for the op-cert verify path

src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:632-646: when required_env is None the require_environment gate at :633 is skipped and _opcert_trust_root is called with required_env=None, which at :503-509 re-enables the envelope_key self-attested fallback that is otherwise withheld under enforcement

Reachability: with require_environment set (hardened) a broken/unreadable rebar.toml transitions to the permissive, envelope_key-accepting state — a fail-open from a configured restriction, distinct from the commit's stated intent of not turning a restriction ON that nobody set
advisory.finding: _required_environment() fails open by catching all exceptions from compose_config and returning None. When an operator has configured verify.require_environment (enforcement ON — the hardened state), a config read/parse failure silently DISABLES the trusted-set restriction on the local claim/close verification path AND re-enables the withheld envelope_key fallback, so an attacker-supplied self-signed cert on the (documented attacker-writable) tickets branch would then certify. compose_config normally propagates ConfigError fail-closed; this call converts that into a permissive downgrade.
scenarios: An operator has flipped the opt-in enforcement pair ON per the runbook, then a config edit temporarily leaves rebar.toml unparseable (or a partial write / IO error occurs) at the moment a cross-environment cert is verified/claimed: enforcement silently lapses and a foreign self-signed cert certifies.

The merge-gate path (verify_required_environment -> opcert.verify_opcert) passes the full keyring and enforces era validity/revocation; the new local path does not, weakening the pinned trust root and applying even when verify.require_environment enforcement is ON.

evidence: `_opcert_signing.py:458-461`: `try: return config.compose_config(root=repo_root).verify.require_environment or None` / `except Exception: ... return None`

`_opcert_signing.py:503-509`: `if required_env is not None: return [], None` — the `envelope_key` fallback (embedded public key from the blob under verification) is withheld ONLY when `required_env is not None`; a `None` result re-enables it.
`_opcert_signing.py:632-642`: the enforcement refusal (`principal != required_env -> foreign_key`) is entirely skipped when `_required_environment` returns `None`.

config.py:514 (compose_config docstring): 'A :class:`ConfigError` propagates (fail-closed startup), exactly as a direct load_config would.' — the rest of the config system is fail-CLOSED on a broken config; `_required_environment` alone catches and downgrades it to the permissive state.

Reachability: on a deployment that has SET `verify.require_environment` (the security-hardening posture), any exception path in `compose_config` (malformed TOML, I/O error, partial write) causes the restriction to evaporate and unpinned `envelope_key` certs (self-signed by any attacker who can write the attacker-writable tickets branch) to certify.
advisory.finding: `_required_environment` fails open: it swallows every exception from `compose_config` and returns `None`, which on the opt-in enforcement path silently disables the `verify.require_environment` trusted-set restriction and re-enables the `envelope_key` fallback. A deployment that opted into enforcement loses it whenever `rebar.toml` is broken or transiently unreadable.
